chapter: Bennie Moten, Basie and the Reno
title: Goodman, Hammond, the Reno Club and later Basie sidemen
summary: Goodwin says Benny Goodman heard Reno Club broadcasts in Chicago and connected Basie with John Hammond. They agree Edison joined in New York and Vic Dickenson joined Basie later.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: Oh Crook -- Baby, we'll get back to you. I wish you'd get down on tape what happened with John Hammond, how he happened to catch Basie's band at the Reno. Wasn't he supposed to catch somebody else?
Well, what happened, Benny Goodman heard the broadcast from the Reno Club; they did broadcasts from there --
Right.
-- and he heard the broadcast from the Reno Club in Chicago.
When Goodman was in Chicago?
Goodman was in Chicago and he flew to Kansas City --
Goodman did?
-- he flew to Kansas City and he's the one that hooked Basie up with John Hammond.
Well, Hammond, of course was Goodman's brother-in-law, but I thought that Hammond was wanting to hear
another band and something happened so --
No.
-- it was either Harlan Leonard's band or --
You've got two things. This was a different thing. When he came here to hear Basie it was Basie that he'd come to hear.
Because Benny Goodman recommended him?

Right, right, fine, and this is how Basie got his start, you know, with the Moten band. You see, at this time all these fellows were not with Basie; Booker Walder and Woody and Mack Washington. They had all left the band.
When did Sweets Edison join the band? It must have been in New York.
It had to be.
Well Vic Dickenson joined it here though didn't he?
No.
Vic joined it in New York too, although he'd been playing around here?
Vic left the band the Kansas City Rockets to go with another band and he was with this band about a year before he joined Basie.
